thread:
ashley: Heads up: saw a 3x p99 latency spike on Mixtral MoE serving yesterday ~03:17 UTC. Traced to router stalls + expert cache churn. Dropping quick notes here before I dig deeper.

cheng: Link to trace (internal): https://internal.perf/trace/2765432109 — flamegraph shows long wait in router::select_topk and a big bump in cuda memcpy for KV swaps.

anika: :eyes: did this line up with any rollout? We had a kernel and router flag change this week.

ashley: Yeah — kernel-v2.14 went out Monday (fp4 optimized kernels) and we also flipped default --router-temp=0.5 for mixtral pools.

matt: Quick repro on bench1: skewed synthetic workload hitting a small hot set. With --router-topk=2 throughput down ~25% but p99 much nicer. With --router-topk=4 throughput up but p99 skyrockets due to cache misses on hot experts.

cheng: Profiling notes: `nvprof --profile-child-processes` shows large H2D memcpy bursts right after router handoff. KV cache eviction rate jumped from ~12% -> ~48% in affected windows.

deploybot: deploybot: kernel-v2.14 deployed to mixtral-prod region-1 at 2026-03-14T02:00Z :white_check_mark:

anika: Hypothesis: the fp4 kernel path modifies RoPE/attention key layout (padding/alignment), which changed the runtime's KV size estimates. Misestimated KV size -> misaligned allocations across expert shards -> extra copies and eviction.

ashley: Also observed rope_scale=0.5 vs 1.0 shifts the seq-len cutoff; sequences >2048 end up on slowpath where router serializes more. So RoPE scaling + kernel layout may be interacting.

cheng: Relevant log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-14T03:17:12Z] router: select_topk start (req=53421)
[2026-03-14T03:17:12Z] kvcache: evict candidate 0x7f9a size=1.2MB
[2026-03-14T03:17:12Z] cuda: memcpy H2D 12.6MB 0.45ms
[2026-03-14T03:17:12Z] router: select_topk end (wait=18.3ms)
```

matt: Proposed mitigation plan: 1) rollback --router-temp to 1.0 on a 10% canary. 2) set --expert-shards=2 on canary to reduce per-expert working set (trade throughput for cache stability). 3) enable `--kv-cache-ttl=30s` vs autodelete to smooth churn.

anika: Also want kernel team to run focused microbench for head/kv dim alignments (8/16 head dims) on fp4 kernels — padding differences can make a big perf cliff.

ashley: Repro command I used (synthetic skewed routing):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"mixtral-moex-8b","prompt":"<hot_user>","rope_scale":0.5,"max_tokens":1024}'
```

cheng: Uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/mixtral/2765432109/trace.tar.gz (flamegraphs, nvprof, pprof dumps).

ashley: Action items: matt -> start canary rollback + set expert_shards on canary. cheng -> extract flamegraphs and correlate with kernel symbols. anika -> ping kernel team & request microbench. I'll watch dashboards and implement short-term throttles if p99 stays high.

matt: :thumbsup: starting rollback now, will report back with canary metrics.

cheng: One more observation: router-v3 introduced a "softfill" topk that probabilistically spreads load. That helped overall variance historically but in this case increases cache line churn when combined with high router-temp, because partially filled experts keep swapping.

anika: If rollback fixes it, we should revert router-temp separately from kernel, so we can isolate cause.

ashley: SGTM. Quick sync in 30m in #eng-runtime to align on canary metrics. Thanks all!
